According to a prominent industry market analyst, God of War Ragnarok is the top-grossing first-party PlayStation game of this console generation.

Rhys Elliott, head of market analysis at Alinea Analytics, took to Twitter to share some new data about God of War Ragnarok's lifetime sales. According to that data, the game has sold 21.6 million copies across PlayStation and Steam, with Steam sales accounting for just 1.6 million of those copies sold. That amounts to $1.4 billion in gross revenue, catapulting it to the top of PlayStation's slate of first-party games for this generation.

As if reading your thoughts, Elliott knows you're wondering how God of War Ragnarok beats out a juggernaut like Marvel's Spider-Man 2, which obviously has massive crossover potential with one of the biggest fandoms in film, TV, and comics. Elliott notes that Marvel's Spider-Man 2 is a PS5 console exclusive, meaning it's not available on PS4 like God of War Ragnarok. That lowers its install base hugely. Also, God of War Ragnarok came out about a year before Marvel's Spider-Man 2, giving it more time to accumulate those sales. Still, God of War Ragnarok wears the PlayStation crown this generation.

"It's another PlayStation evergreen seller, too," Elliott says. "This year, Ragnarok has already sold 1.1M copies, generating nearly $60M (68% on PlayStation), outperforming new 2026 titles like Gears of War E-Day and Saros."

God of War Ragnarok has sold 21.6M copies, as per @alineaanalytics estimates. It's sold 20.1M on PlayStation (75.2% via PS5) and 1.6M on Steam. It's another PlayStation evergreen seller, too. Overall, Ragnarok has been accessed by 6.7M PlayStation Plus players (it was added to the Extra tier about two years ago). So it's performed that well this year DESPITE subscription cannibalisation. That's the pull of God of War IP. That Bautista Series on Amazon is going to be massive - bigger than Fallout, I reckon. As mentioned yesterday, God of War Ragnarok has generated $1.4B, making it the top-grossing first-party PlayStation game of this console generation. Naturally, achieving that sales milestone puts a lot of pressure on Sony Santa Monica to really deliver with God of War Laufey , the next game in its Norse series of God of War games. Notably, God of War Laufey marks a major departure for the series by switching playable characters from Kratos and Atreus to Laufey, Kratos's late wife and Atreus's mother. Having died just before the events of 2018's God of War, Laufey is forced to navigate a world inhabited by fallen gods, which is about as chaotic and violent as you'd expect.

Years after its release, Santa Monica Studio's game continues to find buyers and even outsells many new releases.

God of War: Ragnarok has sold 21.6 million copies, brought Sony about $1.4 billion, and continues to attract new buyers even several years after its release.

According to estimates by analytical firm Alinea Analytics, 20.1 million copies of the game were purchased on PlayStation consoles. Meanwhile, 75.2% of sales on these platforms came from the PS5. Another 1.6 million copies were purchased by Steam users. Total revenue reached approximately $1.4 billion, making the Santa Monica Studio project the most profitable first-party PlayStation Studios game of the current console generation.

The results for 2026 are particularly notable: over this period, God of War: Ragnarok was purchased another 1.1 million times, generating nearly $60 million. Around 68% of this amount came from sales on PlayStation platforms. This year, the game also outsold new releases such as Gears of War: E-Day and Saros.

It should be noted that God of War: Ragnarok has been available to PlayStation Plus Extra subscribers for about two years. Analysts estimate that 6.7 million users have already tried the game through the service. Being in the subscription did not stop the project from continuing to attract buyers. The results show just how long major Sony games can remain profitable after release.

items.title: God of War Laufey delayed to May 2027 in surprise announcement
items.summary: God of War: Laufey has been delayed to May 2027.
items.content:
God of War: Laufey will now launch May 20, 2027.

God of War: Laufey has been delayed in a surprise announcement made today by Santa Monica Studio.

Sony's Santa Monica Studio announced earlier today that it will be delaying the upcoming God of War: Laufey to May 20, 2027.

The original release date for the game was February 16, 2027 when it was announced last year, but this delay will see the game come three months later.

"Since the reveal of God of War Laufey in June, we've been deeply grateful to see so much excitement for Faye's journey through the Everywhen. We don't take for granted the trust placed in our studio to make an extraordinary experience worthy of the passion and dedication of our fans," reads a post by Santa Monica Studio.

"With this in mind, we've made the decision to delay God of War Laufey 's release to May 20th, 2027.

"We will make the most of each moment until then by putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential. On behalf of everyone on the team, we appreciate your patience and we'll be back to share more updates soon!"

God of War: Laufey was originally announced by Sony in June this year , with an announced release date of February 16, 2027.

The game stars Deborah Ann Woll as the titular character Faye, who awakens in a mythological afterlife called the Everywhen following her death prior to God of War (2018). The Everywhen features various gods and deities from across many different theologies, where Faye must find a way home while keeping her husband, Kratos, and son, Atreus, safe from dangerous forces within the Everywhen.

The upcoming game will also feature Jack Quaid as Phranque, a cosmic cube who doesn't remember his past, and Rue, an enchanted ribbon who must prevent a devastatingly powerful sword from falling into the wrong hands, which later becomes Faye's primary weapon.

Developed by Santa Monica Studio, the game acts as both a sequel to God of War and God of War: Ragnarok , while also taking place alongside the events of those games. As the Everywhen is a different dimension where time moves differently, the events of the game are expected to take place both during and after those two games. Although it doesn't star Kratos as the protagonist, he is set to appear in the game.

Topics: God Of War , PlayStation , Santa Monica Studio

items.title: God of War Laufey is delayed, and its new release date has been confirmed: we’ll have to wait a little longer
items.summary: It's official: God of War Laufey has been officially delayed, and its release has been pushed back to May 2027.
items.content:
Santa Monica Studio confirms the date change for the new installment in the series.

The current year isn’t even over yet, and we’ve already seen the first major video game to delay its release. It’s God of War Laufey , a title that was set to come out in mid-February and, following confirmation of the delay, will finally arrive on May 20, 2027 . This isn’t too much of a setback, as it’s only a three-month delay—a period that Santa Monica Studio, as stated in its social media announcement, will use this time “putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential.”

An update regarding God of War Laufey's release date. pic.twitter.com/qCw9O3dqtR

Following the acclaimed God of War (2018) and God of War: Ragnarok, the new God of War: Laufey will put us in the shoes of Laufey (Faye), Kratos’s wife . It will be a journey through Omnitime, a realm beyond the domain of the gods. The game is poised to be PlayStation’s first major AAA release in 2027.

Although there will likely be some new announcements (and perhaps more than a few delays), as of today, we have a truly impressive lineup of new games set to launch in early 2027.

While no specific release dates have been set—though they’re expected in the first few months of 2027—titles include Alien Isolation 2, the Resident Evil CODE: Veronica remake, and Lords of the Fallen 2, among others.

items.title: God of War Laufey Delayed To May 20, 2027
items.summary: Santa Monica Studio has delayed God of War Laufey from February 16 to May 20, 2027, saying the PS5 game starring Faye needs finishing touches.
items.content:
Santa Monica Studio announced Wednesday that the PS5 game starring Faye will now launch on May 20, 2027. The game was set for February 16, 2027, which puts the delay at about three months.

The studio broke the news in a statement posted to its official X account.

“Since the reveal of God of War Laufey in June, we’ve been deeply grateful to see so much excitement for Faye’s journey through the Everywhen. We don’t take for granted the trust placed in the studio to make an extraordinary experience worthy of the passion and dedication of our fans.

“With this in mind, we’ve made the decision to delay God of War Laufey’s release to May 20th, 2027.

“We will make the most of each moment until then by putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential.

“On behalf of everyone on the team, we appreciate your patience and we’ll be back to share more updates soon!”

The February 16 date was announced back in July at San Diego Comic-Con, and pre-orders have been open since September for the Standard and Digital Deluxe editions along with a Collector’s Edition.

It’s also not the first time the studio has moved a God of War game, as God of War Ragnarok slipped from 2021 to 2022.

An update regarding God of War Laufey's release date. pic.twitter.com/qCw9O3dqtR

God of War Laufey is the first mainline entry in the franchise without Kratos in the lead.

Daredevil: Born Again ‘s Deborah Ann Woll voices Faye, Kratos’ wife and Atreus’ mother, who wakes up after her death in the Everywhen, an afterlife for the gods.

Her companions include Phranque, a cosmic cube voiced by Jack Quaid, and Rue, an enchanted ribbon guardian voiced by Perlina Lau.

The game first leaked back in March, when NateTheHate2 reported the next God of War would dump Kratos and star Faye , with a reveal in 2026 and a release in the first half of 2027, “barring any delay.”

The delay happened, and May 20 still lands in the first half of 2027.

items.summary: The awaited God of War game’s PS5 launch has been pushed back. The action-packed title was announced earlier this year during the State of Play broadcast. Santa Monica Studio’s official account recently revealed a message with an “update regarding God of War Laufey’s release date.” The developer has delayed the game, and it won’t come […] The post New God of War Game’s Release Date Gets Delayed, Statement Given appeared first on ComingSoon.net - Movie Trailers, TV & Streaming News, and More .
items.content:
0 Image Credit: Santa Monica Studio The awaited God of War game’s PS5 launch has been pushed back. The action-packed title was announced earlier this year during the State of Play broadcast.

Santa Monica Studio’s official account recently revealed a message with an “update regarding God of War Laufey’s release date.” The developer has delayed the game, and it won’t come out on February 16, 2027. Instead, Laufey will now release on May 20, 2027.

The game will feature a female protagonist, Faye, instead of Kratos, the popular character fans have embraced for years.

Santa Monica’s latest message has clearly revealed that the game has been delayed to “make an extraordinary experience worthy of the passion and dedication” of the fans. Hence, the studio decided to move the PlayStation 5 exclusive to May.

The studio has assured avid fans that it will “make the most of each moment until” the launch “by putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential.” More updates are expected soon ahead of the release.

God of War Laufey will see Faye’s journey through the afterlife of the gods, Everywhen. It’s a place where gods from across mythology fight for the ultimate power. The official description reads, “Awakening unexpectedly in a strange land after her death, Faye discovers the plans she put in place to protect Kratos and Atreus in her absence are now at risk.”

Laufey is directed by Ariel Lawrence. The story will see Deborah Ann Woll reprising her role as Faye after God of War Ragnarök. Other acclaimed actors, including Jack Quaid and Perlina Lau, will play crucial characters. They will assist Faye on her quest, where she also gets to wield legendary weapons during combat.

Originally reported on PlayStation LifeStyle .

Santa Monica Studios has delayed God of War Laufey . The new God of War game for PS5 is no longer set for release in February 2027, and has shifted to May 2027.

Like the previous games , God of War Laufey is a third-person action experience built around chaining together various skills and weapons to dish out tremendous amounts of damage.

Now that the PS6 is getting closer, it's worth looking back at some of the best PS5 games that have been released so far. The 2024 platformer was a love letter to PlayStation's history, with cameos from beloved characters like Nathan Drake and Sackboy.

Astro Bot 's cameos were a ton of fun, but the game had much more to offer than references. Its 90 levels were masterfully designed, and Astro's varied abilities made the game's puzzles a blast to solve. Astro Bot managed to win Game of the Year in 2024, beating out competitors like Balatro and Metaphor: ReFantazio , and that victory was well deserved.

items.title: How to Play the God of War Games in Order
items.summary: Wondering how to play the God of War games in order? We're here to help with a breakdown of the God of War chronology.
items.content:
God of War’s Norse-set masterpieces has cemented it as one of PlayStation’s most iconic franchises . Born during the PS2 era, the God of War franchise made a name for itself with excellent action gameplay, an intriguing tale of divine revenge, and a memorable lead in the Spartan demigod Kratos. 20 years later, God of War has grown into gaming’s seminal action-adventure series, blending that increasingly fine-tuned action with deeper lore and a stronger narrative hook, anchored by an older, more empathic Kratos.

Now that we know the next God of War game will follow Faye in some overlapping timelines, we’ve created this chronology of the series for those interested in playing (or replaying) it from the start.

Sony has released 11 God of War games in the series — seven on home consoles, two on portable consoles, one on mobile, and one text-adventure on Facebook Messenger. A twelfth game, God of War Laufey, was recently announced during a State of Play but does not yet have a release date.

We’re excluding its second mobile release, God of War: Mimir’s Vision, as this AR game doesn’t add to the ongoing narrative but instead provides players with background lore from the world of God of War. We’re also excluding PlayStation All-Stars Battle Royale in this chronology, despite its comical inclusion in the God of War canon .

There are several God of War stories told through novels and comics as well, though this list only includes games.

Although technically the first game in the series chronologically was God of War: Ascension, realistically you'll probably want to start with God of War (2018). Not only is it available on both PS4 and PS5, you can also play it on PC. It's a great starting point for anyone just getting into the series.

These blurbs contain mild spoilers for each game, including characters, settings, and story beats.

God of War Sons of Sparta is the latest game in the series, but chronologically it takes place before any of the others. Sons of Sparta acts as a prequel, following the story of Kratos and his brother Deimos as they undertake their brutal training as Spartans. The gameplay breaks fro mthe usual God of War formula in favor of a retro-inspired Metroidvania style.

Available on : PS5 | IGN's God of War Sons of Sparta Review

Ascension , the seventh God of War game by release date but the first chronologically, is a revenge tale that explores the early days of Kratos’s transformation from a Spartan demigod into the God of War.

Ascension takes place months after Kratos was manipulated into killing his wife and daughter by the Greek God of War Ares (more on this under the original God of War section below). Kratos, traumatized by the killings, refuses to honor the oath he swore to Ares, setting into motion the story of Ascension. Ares seeks revenge through the game’s antagonistic Furies, three beings tasked with punishing betrayal, whom Kratos must kill in order to free himself from his oath. The story ends with Kratos leaving his Spartan home behind, still tormented by his grief.

Available on : PS3 | IGN’s God of War: Ascension Review

Kratos’s next adventure is told in the PSP game aptly named God of War: Chains of Olympus . Olympus takes place halfway through Kratos’s ten-year servitude to the gods (five years before God of War) — a servitude that, once completed, will free him from the torturous visions of his past.

The main plot tasks Kratos with rescuing Helios, the Titan God of the Sun, from the underworld at the behest of Athena. There, he encounters the game’s primary antagonist Persephone, Queen of the Underworld. Persephone presents Kratos with an opportunity to reunite with his daughter, and Kratos wrestles with the apocalyptic repercussions of that reunion and his promise to return Helios to the gods.

items.title: All Of The God Of War Games, Ranked From Worst To Best
items.summary: Before God of War Laufey takes us on Faye’s journey, let’s look back at the ups and downs of Kratos’
items.content:
God of War is about to do something it hasn’t done before: center someone other than Kratos. Before we head into the Everywhen as Faye with God of War Laufey , we thought we’d take a look back at over 20 years of god-slaying and navigating Kratos’ dysfunctional family tree by ranking all the previous games from worst to best. Don’t yell at us if your fave is low on the list. Simply swear vengeance upon us and take out a pantheon of gods on the way.

Mechanically, the 2D, sidescrolling Sons of Sparta maybe wasn’t the kind of treatment I want God of War to get but narratively, yes, please, may I have another. I thought turning GOW into a metroidvania was cute, but the gameplay got tedious after a while. However, I adored that the narrative conceit of the game is Kratos telling his daughter Calliope a story about his life as a child. I have so much grief for Kratos’ first family because they wield so much narrative power over this entire franchise but we know so little about them. Regardless of the gameplay, I’m glad Sons of Sparta exists so I can get my “Kratos being a good dad to his FIRST child for a change” fix. — Ash Parrish

The last PS3 God of War is absolutely a relic of a pre-live-service era when companies were bolting multiplayer modes onto the sides of their most lucrative ships, so it’s not super surprising that the bulk of Ascension feels a little underbaked. The prequel is still full of the kinds of incredible, cinematic set pieces and twitchy action that make each God of War at least memorable, but its hack-and-slash combat feels narrowly focused on Kratos’ iconic Blades of Chaos, with you shifting between different elemental affinities instead of different weapons that would have more tangibly changed up your playstyle and the flow of combat. That final boss fight against the Kraken and the Furies still whips pretty hard, though. — Kenneth Shepard

God of War Ragnarok would have been incredible as two games instead of one. Yeah, the frustratingly bloated and overly long sequel is still rock solid, with fantastic action and some incredible moments, especially for Kratos and Atreus, who remain the heart and soul of the series’ Norse mythology games despite the ever-expanding cast. Still, it’s hard to not get wistful thinking of what this story might’ve looked like if it’d had a bit of breathing room. Ragnarok ’s Valhalla DLC, meanwhile, shows exactly what a hypothetical scaled-back sequel could have looked like by giving Kratos a roguelike therapy session that’s laser-focused on one character instead of a dozen, which helps the core action mechanics shine through in a way that base Ragnarok didn’t, having a bit too much noise going on to let that action sing sometimes. It’s a shame because so many of Ragnarok ’s narrative threads, such as Angrboda seeking out the remnants of the frost giants and the inner machinations of Thor’s family drama, are genuinely compelling, but it’s all fighting for attention in a game that’s trying to wrap up a trilogy’s-worth of stories in a second game. — Kenneth Shepard

The PlayStation Portable was one of the earlier attempts at a handheld offering console-level experiences, and God of War: Chains of Olympus was certainly one of the best examples of a studio making it happen. Ready at Dawn pulled off a handheld God of War remarkably well, creating a Kratos experience that was pretty comparable to its console brethren and that you could take on the go. Though it isn’t quite as narratively illuminating as its sequel, it’s still a truly impressive feat for 2008. — Kenneth Shepard

Ghost of Sparta , Ready at Dawn’s second Chaos Blade swing at a handheld God of War game, is just as solid a game as its predecessor. What gives it a bit of an edge over Chains of Olympus is how much we learn about Kratos in the prequel, including the introduction of his brother Deimos, who adds a whole new wrinkle to Kratos’ dysfunctional family tree. That guy is an onion of layers to peel back, and Ready at Dawn was cooking every time it got the keys to the kitchen. — Kenneth Shepard

Remembering the original God of War 21 years after its 2005 launch feels quaint in a way that makes me uncomfortable with my advancing age. I remember when this game came out; I played it then. But viewing this game now, in the context of what the series has grown into, is bewildering. Voiced by T.C. Carson and equipped with a double jump, this Kratos is a completely different person in a completely different type of game. OG God of War bleeds mid-aughts edginess. The game’s opening shot features a morose Kratos yeeting himself off a cliff, and every female character has her breasts out, just because. That said, the original God of War was a great action platformer with the kind of bloody, violent combat we craved in the mid-aughts. — Ash Parrish

God of War III felt big enough to shoulder the weight of being the “last” major game in the franchise at the time. It contained a “resolution” to Kratos’ story that featured some pretty interesting commentary on the nature and purpose of hope, even if it wasn’t executed that well. God of War III is the franchise’s first flirtation with the “Give Kratos a lil guy to look after” mechanic as Pandora, she of the famous box, tags along for part of your adventure. Chatty sidekicks who help you open doors were already a thing by the time this game came out in 2010, but I wasn’t sure how well the famously dour Kratos would work with the bright and chipper Pandora. And y’know what, he did pretty good. There’s a moment when Zeus hurts Pandora and the camera cuts to Kratos who’s wearing the biggest, ugliest frown, as though all the sliders on his face model were cranked all the way down, and I believed it. I was on his side. — Ash Parrish

God of War II improves on the original in every way with a bigger story and bloodier combat. I really enjoyed the smart, narrative way the game depowers Kratos to set him up to receive new weapons and abilities. Fighting the Colossus of Rhodes, the opening battle in God of War II , is one of the greater gameplay sequences of the PS2 era. Incredibly cinematic and bombastic— you’re fighting the Greek mythological equivalent of a Gundam after all— the fight really conveys what a godly struggle should be, a neat escalation of the mortal battles of the first game. — Ash Parrish

God of War ’s Norse-themed reboot was risky. It changed everything we knew about what it meant to embody Kratos, primarily by acting as a metatextual critique of what the series had once been. A somber, shame-ridden Kratos has retreated to the Nine Realms after slaughtering the Greek pantheon, and rather than flaunting those acts, he attempts to hide them away from his son Atreus before confronting his past and choosing to believe that how things have been is not how they must be. The original God of War games were very much of a different era, one in which edgy, violent excess sold copies. As tastes have changed, God of War had to as well if it was going to thrive, and the 2018 reboot does so not by pretending what came before didn’t happen, but instead by using Kratos’ decade of rage as a springboard to become something greater.

And boy, did it become something greater on the mechanical front, too. Kratos trades his Blades of Chaos (initially) for an icy Leviathan Axe that makes the game feel heavier and more challenging, and the series adopts RPG-lite elements to offer more chances for player expression than the original games were ever capable of. With this reboot, Santa Monica Studio sought to reinvent everything God of War ever was, from its ethos to its best-in-class combat, and it succeeded. — Kenneth Shepard

‘God of War’ Live-Action Cast Guide: Who’s Playing Kratos, Atreus, Thor, Odin and More in the Video Game TV Show
items.summary: See who's who in the 'God of War' live-action video game show coming to Prime Video.
items.content:
One of video games’ most famous and angriest characters is finally being brought to life. PlayStation’s “God of War” series is being adapted by Sony Pictures Television and Amazon Prime Video, and Kratos, Atreus and several of the Norse god characters have been cast.

The upcoming show follows the 2018 “God of War” game, which brought the tragic Greek general Kratos into the frigid Norse wilderness. After brutally killing off nearly every Greek god in PlayStation’s hit video game series, Kratos settles down with a new wife and son, Atreus, in the Norse realm of Midgard. However, after the death of his wife, Kratos is forced to develop a closer bond with his son if they’re to survive attacks from the Norse gods and Ragnarok, the fabled end of the world.

Kratos will be played by Ryan Hurst, who’s recently starred in “The Walking Dead,” “Paradise City” and “The Mysterious Benedict Society.” Hurst is no stranger to the “God of War” video game universe; he voiced Thor in the sequel “God of War: Ragnarok” in 2022. Young newcomer Callum Vinson will star as Atreus, while “Severance” actor Ólafur Darri Ólafsson plays Thor, Mandy Patinkin is Odin and Ed Skrein is Baldur. “God of War” is co-produced by Sony Pictures Television and Amazon MGM Studios in association with PlayStation Productions and Tall Ship Productions.

Prime Video’s series is the first time “God of War” makes the jump to live-action, and it follows the success of the streamer’s other video game show “Fallout.” There’s no lack of video game adaptation on TV or the big screen, with HBO’s “The Last of Us” returning for a third season and films like “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie,” “Street Fighter,” “Resident Evil” and “Mortal Kombat 2” hitting theaters in 2026.

Kratos was first introduced in the 2005 video game “God of War,” set in ancient Greece. He’s a brutal Spartan warrior who was tricked by the god Ares into murdering his own family. Destroyed by grief, Kratos goes on a blood-filled quest for vengeance and murders scores of gods, heroes and monsters across three main games, two spinoffs and a prequel. He’s cursed to wear his family’s ashes on his skin, turning it pale white and earning him the nickname, the Ghost of Sparta. His main weapons are the Blades of Chaos, fiery dual swords that are chained to his wrists.

Eventually, Kratos completes his revenge quest (after surviving an apparent mortal wound in “God of War III”) and settles down in the quiet, snowy Norse realm of Midgard. In the 2018 “God of War” game, he’s remarried to a woman named Faye (who’s recently died) and has a young son named Atreus, who’s weak and must learn survival skills from his father. Instead of his Blades of Chaos, Kratos now wields the Leviathan Axe, which magically returns to him after it’s thrown, much like Thor’s hammer Mjolnir.

Ryan Hurst, known for his roles in “Sons of Anarchy” and “The Walking Dead” on TV and for voicing Thor in “God of War Ragnarok,” brings the video game icon to life in live-action. Terrence C. Carson and Christopher Judge had previously voiced Kratos.

items.content:
• Add more error checking and logging for NVIDIA Streamline

  • When NVIDIAStreamlineLog enabled, a log file in the Save Game directory will be generated and overwritten every launch. If encountering errors, please submit a support ticket including this log. C:\Users\\Saved Games\God of War Ragnarök\sl.log

items.content:
An NVIDIA Driver Crash/Soft Lock that prevents the game from loading is under investigation. In the meantime, we've implemented a work around for the cause of the crash to change how shader compilation works. This change may cause some micro-stuttering during initial load, but will hopefully avoid the driver crash that prevents game from starting.

Please verify files after patching.

items.title: Patch 9 - 20th Anniversary Update
items.summary: As a gift to everyone who owns God of War Ragnarök, the Dark Odyssey collection is now available in-game at no additional cost! Inspired by the working name of God of War (2005) and the skin that originally appeared in God of War II as a re
items.content:
As a gift to everyone who owns God of War Ragnarök, the Dark Odyssey collection is now available in-game at no additional cost! Inspired by the working name of God of War (2005) and the skin that originally appeared in God of War II as a reward for beating the game on God Mode difficulty, we have brought back the black and gold theme for the anniversary.

Dark Odyssey Collection

Dark Odyssey Armor & Appearance for Kratos
  • Dark Odyssey Kratos Appearance
  • Dark Odyssey Armor Set for Kratos (Dark Odyssey Breastplate, Dark Odyssey Bracers, Dark Odyssey Belt)
Dark Odyssey Companion Armor
  • Dark Odyssey Vestment for Atreus
  • Dark Odyssey Witch Frock for Freya
Dark Odyssey Weapon Appearances & Attachments*
  • Dark Odyssey Leviathan Axe & Dark Odyssey Knob
  • Dark Odyssey Blades of Chaos & Dark Odyssey Handles
  • Dark Odyssey Draupnir Spear & Dark Odyssey Hind
Dark Odyssey Shield Appearances & Rönd
  • Dark Odyssey Guardian Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Dauntless Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Stone Wall Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Shatter Start Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Onslaught Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Spartan Aspis Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Rönd
*Please note, the weapon appearances are made for the fully upgraded version of each weapon and will only be available for use upon reaching that upgrade.

Edit Appearance for Weapon & Shield Attachments

With the addition of the new Dark Odyssey weapon attachments and shield rönd in the patch, we have added the ability to use the ‘Edit Appearance’ feature on those components of Kratos’ arsenal. You’ll be able to pick whatever visual suits your look with the functionality you want for your build!
